primary_claim: A tokenizer-normalized perplexity metric (Weighted Perplexity Benchmark) shows that raw tokenization differences can affect apparent language-model perplexity comparisons by up to 21.6% (largest for Mixtral models), and after normalizing for this, Llama 4 Scout performs substantially worse on WikiText-2 than models with far fewer active parameters.

effect.metric: % change in perplexity from tokenizer normalization

contradicts_or_qualifies: Provides a computationally simple alternative to marginal-tokenization normalization (Cao & Rimell 2021), which requires significant computational overhead
stated_future_work: Extend validation to multiple datasets and languages
Test a broader set of models
Validate the method with independent implementations
Assess the relevance of perplexity by finding its relationship with other benchmarks
limitations_stated: Results are demonstrated only on WikiText-2; generalization across domains and languages requires validation
A limited set of tested models limits statistical confidence
Conclusions about MoE architectural efficiency rest on limited examples (Llama Scout, Mixtral)
quote: we demonstrate how tokenization differences can affect traditional perplexity measurements by up to 21.6%.
